draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Alappuzha Beach! The old pier running out into the sea here is over 150 years old, and back when it was used for trade it carried three railway lines. The town behind you is laced with canals, which is why people call it the Venice of the East.
draft.hungryLine: There's cheap South Indian food and coffee right on the beach, and good bakes a short ride into town.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk down to the beach and the old pier, then over to the 1862 lighthouse. Both are under 20 minutes on foot from here.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stroll the beach promenade with an ice cream or some peanuts from the stalls and watch the locals play frisbee and volleyball.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Pliny the Elder mentioned this place way back in the 1st century AD, calling it Baraces.

spots.name: Alappuzha Beach
spots.detail: 16 min walk · Big, flat beach with the old trading pier

spots.name: Alappuzha Lighthouse
spots.detail: 17 min walk · Built in 1862, the first on Kerala's Arabian Sea coast

spots.name: Maqam Masjid
spots.detail: 16 min walk · Mid-1800s mosque by the Vadakanal canal

legends.title: The payasam nobody can copy
legends.body: The Sreekrishna Swamy Temple's paal-payasam recipe is a well guarded secret. People believe the same cooks can't make it taste the same anywhere else, because the Lord blessed his favourite kitchen.

legends.title: A church from St. Thomas
legends.body: St. Mary's Church at Champakulam is believed to be one of the seven churches St. Thomas set up. Alleppey still has a lot of Christians today.

tips.title: Don't swim here.
tips.body: The water is deep and the currents are strong, even more so during and after the monsoon.

tips.title: Book houseboats with operators, not touts.
tips.body: Book online if you can, and don't leave it to the last minute in high season.

story.title: Baraces
story.body: Alappuzha goes back to the Sangam era. Pliny the Elder wrote about it as Baraces nearly 2,000 years ago.

story.title: Spice town
story.body: The town grew into an important hub for trading spices. The Dutch and the Portuguese both came here to do business.

story.title: Port and canals
story.body: Under Raja Kesavadas, a port was built and canals were dug through the city for transport. The town grew fast. By the late 1700s it was under British rule and its trade began to fade.

story.title: A light on the coast
story.body: The Alappuzha Lighthouse went up in 1862, the first of its kind on Kerala's Arabian Sea coast. It still draws visitors today.

story.title: Snake boats
story.body: Jawaharlal Nehru opened the snake boat race in 1952, and it's named after him. It's held on the second Saturday of August, with around a hundred people in each boat.

food.name: Indian Coffee House
food.detail: Right on the beach · Cheap South Indian food, ice cream and their signature coffee

food.name: Dreamers
food.detail: On the beach front · Well-priced Indian food, grab a table on the bamboo terrace

food.name: Himalaya Bakery
food.detail: Mullackal Road · Puffs, samosas and a lovely banana walnut cake
